SUPO, where required) WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS: As a Quality Assurance Technician you are the independent set of eyes between our production line and orbit. You will perform in-process and final inspections of electronic and mechanical assemblies, verify that every integration step is carried out to procedure, and carry out the final inspection of completed satellites before they leave for environmental testing and launch. You will witness mandatory inspection points (MIPs), confirm workmanship against IPC and ECSS requirements, check torque, bonding, harness routing, connector mating and cleanliness, and make sure the build record is complete and audit-ready. Embedded within the production and AIT (Assembly, Integration and Test) environment, you will work in cleanrooms with ESD-sensitive flight hardware. Working closely with Production, AIT Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Mission Assurance and Supply Chain, you will catch defects before they move downstream, prevent quality escapes, and help every satellite we ship meet space-grade standards. The supply chain teams of our sister companies in Spain, Poland, Germany and Greece will also report to you. The vendors who claim to know are mostly wrong. So we're setting up a five-person skunkworks in Valencia to find out, by building real hardware with AI - outside of the program schedules with a pure focus on finding the things that “move the needle”. You'll hire the team of four or five builders and build alongside them. "Lead" here means first builder. You get a room next to the lab and a budget you spend without an approval process, and the team keeps two standing obligations: build something every week and show it to the rest of ICEYE every month.
